mainTopic: Can a law learned through one method of Torah derivation (היקש, גזירה שוה) go on to teach another case through a further method?
overview: The amud opens by closing an earlier question with a teaching of דבי רבי ישמעאל. The גמרא then asks a series of questions about chains of learning: can a law learned by one method go on to teach through another? First it asks about a law learned by היקש teaching through a בנין אב. רבי ירמיה tries to prove from the north rule for אשם that it cannot, but the proof is rejected, because each offering, alone or paired with another, has a special feature. Next, רב פפא shows that a law learned by גזירה שוה can teach by היקש: the מעשר-money rule passes from שלמים to תודה, and רבינא defends this against מר זוטרא. Finally the גמרא asks whether a law learned by גזירה שוה can teach through another גזירה שוה. רמי בר חמא's proof from the תודה breads is knocked down by רבינא. רבא then starts a new proof from the bull of the כהן גדול, which is cut up like an עולה but not skinned, and links it to the bull and goat of יום כפור; that proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier question is answered from a teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of a previous discussion: the answer to the earlier question is clear from a teaching of דבי רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is clear from what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier discussion that began before this text. It says the answer comes from a known teaching of דבי רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is not a new topic. It closes the previous question by pointing to a teaching already discussed earlier in the מסכתא. Once it is closed, the גמרא is free to ask the next question in its series.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the study house of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: From that which the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion that began before this text.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The previous inquiry is resolved from a teaching of דבי רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: Can a law learned by juxtaposition teach through a paradigm?
steps.stepSummary: New question: if a law was learned through a היקש, can it then teach that law to another case through a בנין אב?
steps.simpleTranslation: A law that was learned through a juxtaposition: can it then teach through a paradigm?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about the rules of Torah learning. Something was learned by a היקש. Can it now become the source for a בנין אב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A היקש links two topics because the Torah places them side by side. A בנין אב takes one case as a model and applies its law to similar cases. The question is whether a law that only came through a היקש is strong enough to serve as that model.

keyTerms.meaning: Juxtaposition: two topics the Torah places together, so they share laws
Paradigm: one case serves as the model for similar cases
A matter that was itself learned from somewhere else
What is the law? (opens a question)

steps.confusionAlert: Here the היקש is what the source learned. The בנין אב is what the source would now teach. Keep straight which method came first.

phrases.english: A matter that is learned through a juxtaposition,
what is the law: may it teach through a paradigm?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ, מַהוּ שֶׁיְּלַמֵּד בְּבִנְיַן אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next question in a series about which methods of derivation can pass a law onward.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a law derived by היקש can serve as the source of a בנין אב.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה proves it cannot, from the north rule written for the guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה argues that the Torah would not need to write the north rule for אשם if it could be learned from חטאת by בנין אב. So something learned by היקש cannot teach by בנין אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: The Torah should not have written 'north' for the guilt offering. We could have learned it by paradigm from the sin offering. Why did it write it? Doesn't this show that something learned by juxtaposition cannot go on to teach by paradigm?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה tries to answer the question by proving the answer is no. He points to a verse that would be extra if the answer were yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The north rule for חטאת is itself learned through a היקש to עולה. If חטאת could pass this rule to אשם by בנין אב, the Torah's separate verse for אשם would be unnecessary. Since the Torah wrote it anyway, it must be that חטאת, having learned by היקש, cannot teach by בנין אב.

keyTerms.meaning: To the north: קדשי קדשים must be slaughtered in the northern part of the עזרה
Guilt offering
Sin offering
For what law did the Torah write it? (asks why a verse is needed)
It cannot turn around and teach

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the standard Talmudic proof style: a verse would be extra, so its presence tells us a rule about how derivations work.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Let the Torah not write 'north' regarding a guilt offering,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:2

phrases.english: and let it be derived by paradigm from a sin offering;
for what law did it write it?
Is it not to say
that a matter learned through a juxtaposition
phrases.notes: This is about the חטאת: its north rule was itself learned from the עולה through a היקש.

phrases.english: does not go on to teach through a paradigm?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: לָא לִכְתּוֹב צָפוֹנָה בְּאָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 with a proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a law learned by היקש cannot teach through a בנין אב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah's separate verse requiring the north for אשם, which would be extra if חטאת could teach it by בנין אב.

steps.title: The proof fails, because the sin offering has a unique feature
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Even עולה cannot teach אשם by בנין אב, because עולה is completely burned. In the same way, חטאת cannot teach it, because it atones for sins punished by כרת. So the verse for אשם is needed anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: But by your logic, learn it by paradigm from the burnt offering! Why can't we? Because we can object: the burnt offering is special because it is completely burned. The sin offering can be objected to also: it is special because it atones for sins punished by כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי ירמיה's proof. It shows the verse for אשם would be needed for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולה's north rule is written outright, yet it still cannot teach אשם, because עולה has something אשם lacks (כליל). That shows a special feature blocks a בנין אב. חטאת also has a feature אשם lacks: it atones for כריתות. So the verse for אשם may be written only because of that difference, and nothing is proven about היקש.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turns the speaker's logic back on him)
Burnt offering
One can refute it (point out a difference that blocks the comparison)
Entirely burned on the מזבח
Sins punishable by כרת

steps.confusionAlert: The question about עולה is not a real suggestion to learn from עולה. It sets up the comparison: just as עולה is blocked by a difference, so is חטאת.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
let it be derived by paradigm from a burnt offering!
What is the reason it cannot be derived?
Because one can refute it:
What about a burnt offering? It is special in that it is entirely burned;
a sin offering can also be refuted:
What about a sin offering?
It is special in that it atones for sins punishable by karet.
phrases.notes: אשם does not atone for sins punishable by כרת, so the two offerings are not alike.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, תֵּיתֵי מִבִּנְיַן אָב מֵעוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי ירמיה's proof in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. The question of step 2 stays open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The verse for אשם is needed anyway, because חטאת has a unique feature (atoning for כריתות) that blocks any בנין אב from it.

steps.title: Learn the guilt offering from two offerings together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא revives the proof. No single offering can teach אשם, but עולה and חטאת together could. So the verse for אשם still looks extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: One cannot be learned from one. Let one be learned from two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי ירמיה's proof against the objection. It suggests learning אשם from two offerings together instead of from one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source alone has a weakness: עולה is כליל and חטאת atones for כריתות. Put together, their shared feature (both need the north) can teach אשם, since each one's weakness is missing from the other. If so, the Torah's separate verse for אשם is extra again, and the proof that חטאת, learned by היקש, cannot teach is back in play.

keyTerms.meaning: One from one: learning a case from a single source
One from two: learning a case from two sources combined
It cannot be derived

steps.whatToRemember: The defense of רבי ירמיה's proof now depends on learning one offering from the other two together (עולה plus חטאת). Steps 6–8 test this and reject every pairing, so this revival does not stand.

phrases.english: One from one cannot be derived;
let one be derived from two!
phrases.notes: The two are the עולה and the חטאת, which together would teach the north rule to the אשם.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מֵחֲדָא – לָא אָתְיָא; תֵּיתֵי חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection of step 4 and restores the proof of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Offers a two-source בנין אב that avoids each single source's weakness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since each offering alone has a unique feature, the verse for אשם was needed, so there is no proof.
steps.terutzMaskana: Combined, עולה and חטאת could teach אשם, so the verse is extra again and the proof returns.

steps.title: The burnt offering cannot be learned from the sin and guilt offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which offering could be learned from the other two. It tries learning עולה from חטאת and אשם, but those two atone, so the attempt fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: From which offering would you learn it? Should the Torah skip the north rule for עולה and let us learn it from חטאת and אשם? No, because those two are special: they atone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 5's idea that two offerings together can teach the third. It starts by testing whether עולה could be learned from חטאת and אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For two cases to teach a third, the third case must not lack any special feature that the two share. חטאת and אשם both atone for sins in a way עולה does not. So they cannot teach עולה, and the verse about עולה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: From which would it come? (Which case would be learned from the others?)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
What about these? (They have something special)
They atone (for sins)

phrases.english: From which would it come?
phrases.notes: He means: out of the three offerings, which one could you learn from the other two?

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write it about the burnt offering,
and let it come from the sin offering and the guilt offering?
What about these?
They are special in that they atone.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵהֵי תֵּיתֵי? לָא נִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא עוֹלָה, וְתֵיתֵי מֵחַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 5's claim that two offerings together could teach the third.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: First of three tests showing that the two-together derivation fails for every offering.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חטאת and אשם share atonement, which עולה lacks.

steps.title: The sin offering cannot be learned from the burnt and guilt offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries learning חטאת from עולה and אשם. Those two come only from male animals, so the attempt fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should the Torah skip the rule for חטאת and let us learn it from the other two? No, because those two are special: they are males.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second pairing, learning חטאת from עולה and אשם, and rejects it as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולה and אשם are both brought only from male animals. A private person's חטאת is a female animal. Because of this difference, the verse about חטאת is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Males (male animals)
These (the other two offerings)

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write it about the sin offering,
and let it come from these?
phrases.notes: These are the עולה and the אשם.

phrases.english: What about these? They are special in that they are males.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּחַטָּאת, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second pairing in the same series of tests.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Shows חטאת cannot be learned from עולה and אשם.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: עולה and אשם are only males; a private חטאת is female.

steps.title: The guilt offering cannot be learned from the burnt and sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries learning אשם from עולה and חטאת. Those two are brought by the community as well as by individuals, so the attempt fails, and the proof falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should the Torah skip the rule for אשם and let us learn it from the other two? No, because those two are special: they are brought by the community just as by an individual.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the last pairing, learning אשם from עולה and חטאת, and rejects it too. With this, Step 5's revival fails completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולה and חטאת can be brought by the whole community, but an אשם is only ever brought by an individual. So no offering can be learned from the other two, and every north verse, including the one for אשם, is needed. That means the אשם verse is not extra, and רבי ירמיה's proof still does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: The community (offerings brought for all of Israel)
An individual person

steps.whatToRemember: Each pair of offerings has a special feature the third lacks: atonement, being male, being brought by the community. So the Torah had to write the north rule for each one, and the question of whether something learned by היקש can teach by בנין אב is not settled by this proof.

phrases.english: Let it not be written about the guilt offering,
and let it come from these?
phrases.notes: These are the עולה and the חטאת.

phrases.english: What about these?
They are special in that they exist for the community as for an individual.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נִכְתּוֹב בְּאָשָׁם, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final pairing; completes the rejection of Step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Knocks out Step 5's revival entirely, so רבי ירמיה's proof (Step 3) is rejected again.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: עולה and חטאת are brought by the community; אשם never is.

steps.title: Can something learned by verbal analogy teach by juxtaposition?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: if a law was learned through a גזירה שוה, can it then pass that law on to another case through a היקש?
steps.simpleTranslation: A matter learned through a גזירה שוה: can it teach through a היקש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question in the same series about chains of derivation. This line sets up the question, and the answer follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the question was about היקש followed by בנין אב. Now the order of tools changes: first a גזירה שוה, then a היקש. The גמרא wants to know whether a law that came in through one method can travel on through the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching drawn from the same word appearing in two places in the Torah
A teaching drawn from two topics placed side by side in the Torah
A matter that was itself learned (from somewhere else)

phrases.english: A matter that is learned through a verbal analogy,
what is the law, may it teach through a juxtaposition?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה, מַהוּ שֶׁיְּלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question in the same pattern as Step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a law learned by גזירה שוה can be passed on through a היקש.

steps.title: רב פפא: the thanks offering may be bought with tithe money
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings the verse that places תודה right next to שלמים. Since שלמים may be bought with מעשר money, the היקש teaches that תודה may be too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The verse says, "And this is the law of the peace offering... if for a thanks offering." From here we learned that a תודה may come from מעשר money, because we found that שלמים may come from מעשר money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers yes. He shows a case where a law passes from שלמים to תודה through a היקש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse joins תודה to שלמים, which is a היקש. The rule that שלמים may be bought with מעשר money is passed on to תודה through that היקש. The way the question is framed implies that the שלמים rule was itself learned by גזירה שוה, so a law learned by גזירה שוה does go on to teach by היקש.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanks offering
Peace offering
Tithe; here, the money from redeeming the second tithe (מעשר שני)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rules for chaining derivations depend on which tools are involved. Here, גזירה שוה followed by היקש is allowed.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
"And this is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings [etc.]
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:11–12. The word in square brackets means "and so on"; the verse keeps going.

phrases.english: if for a thanks offering"
we learned that a thanks offering may come from tithe money,
since we found that peace offerings come from tithe money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The מעשר-money rule passes from שלמים (implied to be learned by גזירה שוה) to תודה through the היקש of the verse.

steps.title: Where שלמים Get Their מעשר Rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that שלמים may be bought with מעשר שני money because of a גזירה שוה on the word 'שם'. So the rule passed to תודה was itself learned by גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that שלמים themselves may be bought with מעשר money? Because the word 'there' is written by both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof from step 10. It shows that the שלמים rule, which was passed to תודה, was itself learned through a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 תודה learned from שלמים through a היקש. Now we see that שלמים learned their own rule from מעשר שני through a גזירה שוה on the word 'שם'. So a law learned by גזירה שוה went on to teach by היקש, which answers the question from step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a law from one case to another because the same word appears in both
Themselves
From where do we know?
'There.' This is the shared word that links the two verses

steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the answer to step 9. A law learned by גזירה שוה can be passed on by היקש.

phrases.english: And the peace offerings themselves, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know that שלמים may be bought with מעשר money?

phrases.english: As it is written "there" and "there."
phrases.notes: דברים 27:7 (שלמים) and דברים 14:23 (מעשר שני).

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלָמִים גּוּפַיְיהוּ מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's proof by showing that the source rule was itself learned by גזירה שוה
steps.raayaObject: That a law learned by גזירה שוה can teach by היקש
steps.raayaSupportSource: The 'שם'/'שם' גזירה שוה between שלמים and מעשר שני, followed by the היקש of תודה to שלמים

steps.title: Objection: מעשר Is Not Holy
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא challenges the proof. מעשר דגן is only חולין, so this case says nothing about the rules of קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא son of רב מרי said to רבינא: grain tithe is just ordinary, non-holy food!
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא attacks the proof. The original source of the law, מעשר, is not a holy offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against passing a learned law on to another case applies to קדשים. Since the starting point here is מעשר, which counts as חולין, he argues the proof does not show anything about קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: The tithe of grain, which includes מעשר שני
Ordinary, non-holy food or items
Merely, just

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Mari, said to Ravina:
The tithe of grain is merely non-sacred!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב מָרִי לְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof just completed
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from מעשר, שלמים and תודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule is about קדשים, but מעשר is חולין. So this case may not count as a learned law passing on within קדשים.

steps.title: Only the Learner Needs to Be Holy
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the rule never required both sides to be holy. It is enough that the case doing the learning, שלמים, is קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did the one who said this rule say it only when both the case that learns and the case that teaches are holy?! No, it is enough that the one that learns is holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא defends the proof. He asks a pointed question to show that the teaching side does not have to be holy too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on the case doing the learning being קדשים. שלמים are קדשים, so once they learn from מעשר, their law counts as a law learned within קדשים. When it then passes on to תודה, the proof stands, even though מעשר itself is חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: The case that learns, meaning the one receiving the law
The case that teaches, meaning the source of the law
Holy, part of קדשים

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as רבינא agreeing with מר זוטרא. His question is rhetorical, and the expected answer is 'no'. The teaching side does not need to be holy.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof stands: a law learned by גזירה שוה can be passed on by היקש in קדשים.

phrases.english: He said to him: Did the one who said it say it
phrases.notes: Literally 'the one who said it, said it'. This is the rule that a learned law in קדשים can't teach again.

phrases.english: only where the learner is holy and the teacher is holy?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, אָמַר אָמְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר זוטרא's objection
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule applies only when both the source and the learning case are קדשים
steps.terutzMaskana: It is enough that the learning case (שלמים) is קדשים

steps.title: Can a גזירה שוה Pass On Through Another גזירה שוה?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: if a law was learned by גזירה שוה, can it then teach another case through a second גזירה שוה?
steps.simpleTranslation: A law learned through a גזירה שוה: can it go on to teach through another גזירה שוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question in the same series. This time both links in the chain are a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the second link was a היקש. Now the גמרא asks about a chain of two גזירה שוה links, which is a different kind of case and needs its own proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A law that was itself learned from somewhere else
What is the law?

phrases.english: A matter learned through a verbal analogy,
what is the law, may it teach through a verbal analogy?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה, מַהוּ שֶׁיְּלַמֵּד בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the next question in the series, now with a second גזירה שוה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a law learned by גזירה שוה can teach through another גזירה שוה in קדשים

steps.title: רמי בר חמא Begins: Poached Loaves Come From Fine Flour
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא starts his answer with a ברייתא. The phrase 'סלת מורבכת' teaches that the רבוכה loaves of the תודה are made of fine flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: a ברייתא teaches that from 'fine flour, poached' we learn that the poached loaves come from fine flour.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא begins answering the new question by quoting a ברייתא. This is the first piece of his proof, and the rest is still coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first sets up a basic fact: the רבוכה loaves of the תודה must be fine flour, learned straight from the פסוק. The proof will build a chain of learning from this starting point.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine flour
Poached, meaning scalded in hot water and then cooked with oil. This is one type of the תודה loaves
We have learned

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said: It was taught in a baraita:
"Fine flour, poached"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12, about the loaves brought with a תודה.

phrases.english: We have learned that the poached loaves come from fine flour.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא, תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Opens a proof from a ברייתא about the תודה loaves. The ברייתא continues in step 16.

steps.title: The loaves and wafers of the תודה get their fine-flour rule step by step
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The חלות learn fine flour from the רבוכה through the word 'חלות', and the רקיקין then learn it from the חלות through the word 'מצות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we know the loaves need fine flour? The Torah says 'loaves' and 'loaves'. Where do we know the wafers need it? The Torah says 'matzos' and 'matzos'.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא finishes his ברייתא. It shows a chain: one item learns from another, and that second item had itself only learned the rule through a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבוכה are explicitly fine flour. The חלות learn this from them through a גזירה שוה on 'חלות'. Then the רקיקין learn it from the חלות through a second גזירה שוה on 'מצות'. That second link is exactly the case the question in Step 14 was asking about: a law learned by גזירה שוה teaching again by גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Thick loaves, one of the bread types brought with the תודה
Thin wafers, another bread type of the תודה
Unleavened breads; this is the word that links the wafers to the loaves
'The verse teaches'; it introduces the source

phrases.english: The loaves, from where do we know they are fine flour?
The verse says: 'loaves' and 'loaves'.
phrases.notes: Both are in ויקרא 7:12. The רבוכה are also called 'חלות', and they are clearly fine flour.

phrases.english: The wafers, from where do we know?
The verse says: 'matzos' and 'matzos'.
phrases.notes: In ויקרא 7:12 the loaves are 'חלות מצות' and the wafers are 'רקיקי מצות'. So the wafers learn from the loaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַלּוֹת מִנַּיִין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun in Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The רקיקין learn by גזירה שוה from the חלות, which themselves learned by גזירה שוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the actual case that would prove the rule. Everything in the next step depends on whether this chain really holds.

steps.title: Maybe the wafers learn from the oven-baked offering instead
steps.stepSummary: רבינא argues the word 'מצות' could come from the מנחת מאפה תנור, where fine flour is stated outright, so the ברייתא proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to him: How do you know the 'matzos'–'matzos' link learns from the loaves? Maybe it learns from the oven-baked offering!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רמי בר חמא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מצות' also appears in the מנחת מאפה תנור in ויקרא 2:4, and there fine flour is written directly. If the רקיקין learn from there, they learn from a plainly written law, not from a learned one. Then there is no chain of two גזירות שוות, and the proof falls.

keyTerms.meaning: An oven-baked flour offering (ויקרא 2:4)
'He learns'; the source a derivation comes from
'Perhaps'; it introduces another possibility

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying the wafers don't need fine flour. They still do. He only questions which source they learn it from.

phrases.english: Ravina said to him:
From where do you know that 'matzos'–'matzos'
learns from the loaves?
Perhaps it learns from the oven-baked offering!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:4. There fine flour is written right in the verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא: מִמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in Steps 15–16
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's proof from the תודה breads
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different source for 'מצות' explains the ברייתא, so it never needs a 'learned-from-learned' chain.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רמי בר חמא's proof only. The wafers still need fine flour, and the question of step 14 stays unanswered until רבא's new source in step 18.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'מצות'–'מצות' link may come from the מנחת מאפה תנור (ויקרא 2:4), where fine flour is written outright. If so, the wafers learn from a written law, not from a learned one, and there is no chain of two גזירות שוות.

steps.title: רבא brings a new source: the bull is carried out whole
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא about the bull of the כהן גדול. The verse teaches that it is carried out of the camp whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: a ברייתא teaches that 'its innards and its dung, he shall carry out' shows he takes it out whole.
steps.whatsHappening: After רמי בר חמא's proof falls, רבא starts a new proof. This line sets up the base fact that the next line builds on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bull of the כהן גדול is burned outside the camp. The verse mentions its innards and dung going out together with it, which shows the whole animal is carried out in one piece. The ברייתא will next ask how it is burned.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather'; it drops the last answer and offers a new one
Its innards
Its dung
Whole, in one piece

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: it was taught in a ברייתא:
'And its innards and its dung, he shall carry out'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:11–12, about the bull of the כהן גדול.

phrases.english: This teaches that he carries it out whole.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא, תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that רבינא rejected
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Begins a new source to answer the question of Step 14

steps.title: The bull is burned in pieces, learned from the עולה
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה on 'ראשו וכרעיו' teaches that, just like the עולה, the bull is burned only after being cut into pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he burns it whole. It says here 'its head and its legs', and it says there 'its head and its legs'. Just as there it is done by cutting into pieces, so too here.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It teaches that the bull is cut up before burning, and it learns this from the עולה through a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could suggest burning the bull whole, the same way it was carried out. The shared words 'ראשו וכרעיו' link it to the עולה, which the Torah clearly says is cut into pieces. Now the cutting law for the bull is itself a law learned by גזירה שוה, which sets up רבא's chain.

keyTerms.meaning: Cutting the animal into its pieces
'Its head and its legs'; the shared words that link the two cases
'One might think'; it raises a possible mistake to reject
'There'; the other case being compared

steps.whyThisMatters: The bull's cutting law is now a learned law. That makes it the base for a further derivation that proves the rule of Step 14.

phrases.english: One might think he burns it whole?
It is said here: 'its head and its legs',
and it is said there: 'its head and its legs';
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:12–13, about the עולה.

phrases.english: just as there it is done by cutting into pieces,
so too here it is done by cutting into pieces.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִשְׂרְפֶנּוּ שָׁלֵם? נֶאֱמַר כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That the bull's burning-in-pieces law comes through a גזירה שוה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's גזירה שוה of 'ראשו וכרעיו' from the עולה

steps.title: Should the bull also be skinned like an עולה?
steps.stepSummary: If the bull learns from the עולה that it is cut into pieces, maybe it should also learn that it is skinned first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then just as there (the עולה) is skinned, here too (the bull) should also be skinned!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on its own comparison. If the bull is like the עולה for cutting, maybe it is also like the עולה for skinning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה links two cases, so we might expect it to carry over all the details. The עולה is skinned (הפשט) before it is cut up. So the question is whether the bull must be skinned too.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as over there, meaning in the other case being compared
So too here, meaning in our case
Skinning an animal, removing its hide

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if we compare the bull to the עולה, as the last step did.

phrases.english: just as there it is with skinning,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the עולה, which is skinned before it is cut up.

phrases.english: so too here it should also be with skinning?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי – מָה לְהַלָּן בְּהֶפְשֵׁט, אַף כָּאן נָמֵי בְּהֶפְשֵׁט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the גזירה שוה from step 19 should reach
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of the bull to the עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bull matches the עולה for cutting, it should match it for skinning too

steps.title: The verse 'its innards and its dung' rules out skinning
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the פסוק 'וקרבו ופרשו' that the bull is not skinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And its innards and its dung.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge by quoting a פסוק about the bull. It does not yet explain how the פסוק shows this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison to the עולה is limited by the bull's own פסוק. So the bull is cut up like an עולה, but its own verse blocks the skinning. How the verse teaches this is left for the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches, used to bring a פסוק that settles the point
Its innards
Its dung, the waste inside the animal

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And its innards and its dung."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:11

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְקִרְבּוֹ וּפִרְשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק that limits the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bull should be skinned like the עולה
steps.terutzMaskana: The bull's own פסוק shows it is not skinned

steps.title: How does this verse teach it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the words 'וקרבו ופרשו' show that the bull is not skinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the lesson learned from it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: how do these words prove there is no skinning? This sets up רב פפא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse only lists innards and dung, and says nothing openly about skin. So the גמרא wants to know how we get 'no skinning' out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the lesson? How is it learned from the verse?

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּלְמוּדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the verse quoted in step 21 works
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How 'וקרבו ופרשו' shows the bull is not skinned

steps.title: רב פפא: the flesh stays in its skin like the dung stays inside
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains: just as the dung stays inside the animal when it is burned, so the flesh stays inside its skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Just as its dung is inside its innards, so its flesh stays in its skin.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains the verse. The bull is burned with the dung still inside, and in the same way the meat is burned still in its skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody takes the dung out of the bull before burning it. רב פפא reads the verse as a model: the skin also stays on the flesh. So the bull is cut into pieces like an עולה, but it is not skinned.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too, setting up a comparison
Its flesh in its skin, meaning not skinned

steps.whatToRemember: The פר כהן גדול is cut into pieces like an עולה (from the גזירה שוה), but it is not skinned (from 'וקרבו ופרשו'). For רבא's proof, the key point is that its cutting law is a law learned by גזירה שוה. The next step begins רבי's ברייתא, which passes that law on through a second גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Just as its dung is inside its innards,
so its flesh is in its skin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁפִּרְשׁוֹ בְּקִרְבּוֹ, כָּךְ בְּשָׂרוֹ בְּעוֹרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dung stays inside when burned, and the flesh likewise stays in its skin, so there is no skinning

steps.title: רבא brings רבי's ברייתא on the bull and goat of יום כפור
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a second ברייתא. רבי points out that the verse about the יום כפור bull and goat mentions skin, flesh and dung.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: רבי says: It is stated here 'skin, flesh and dung'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a second ברייתא to build his proof. This line only sets up רבי's teaching, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Here' means the bull and goat of יום כפור. Their verse uses the same words, skin, flesh and dung, that appear about the bull of the כהן גדול. That word match lets רבי link the two cases. The link itself comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Skin, flesh and dung, the words from the יום כפור verse

phrases.english: And it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi says:
It is stated here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the bull and goat of יום כפור, ויקרא 16:27.

phrases.english: skin and flesh [and dung],
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets; it's part of the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן עוֹר וּבָשָׂר וָפֶרֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא to רבא's answer after the first ברייתא is finished
steps.raayaObject: That a law learned by גזירה שוה (the cutting into pieces of the כהן גדול's bull, learned from the עולה) can teach through a second גזירה שוה (to the bull and goat of יום כפור, via 'עור ובשר ופרש').
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי on the פר and שעיר of יום כפור (ויקרא 16:27)
